commentary_segments.text: To illustrate once more what the difference is between an amplifier and a transconductor, the transfer curve is illustrated for several of them. An amplifier has high gain and a small input range. A bipolar-transistor amplifier is a good example. A transconductor has low gain but a large input range. A MOST amplifier with large V −V values and a GS T bipolar-transistor amplifier with emitter resistors, are good examples. Real transconductors have an even larger input range. Their range is extended by means of linearization techniques such as local feedback and cross-coupling. They are now studied.
